Contract status

FHR contract status
StatusReleased contract. schemaVersion "2.1" shipped in shared specification v0.6.0 on 2026-11-13.
Versions this schema accepts2.0, 2.1. A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state any earlier minor of the same major, and holds each of them to that minor: what a later minor allows is invalid in an earlier one.
What it describesFHR is the FAIR-bioHeaders header for a reference genome assembly. It travels as a ;~ YAML block at the top of the assembly FASTA file, as a #~ block at the top of a GFA file, or standalone as JSON or YAML, and one SHA-512/256 checksum ties the metadata to the exact bytes of that file.
What it does not coverFHR describes the assembly as a resource: what it is called, which species it is, who assembled it, who wrote the header, when, how it was made and under what conditions it may be reused. It does not describe individual sequences, does not carry annotation, and does not certify biological quality.

Serializations with verified support

  • FASTA (;~ header block) and GFA (#~ header block): the shared rules R1 to R14 in docs/FORMAT.md, implemented by the toolkit.
  • Standalone JSON and YAML metadata files, read and written by the toolkit.
  • JSON-LD: a canonical FHR form with an embedded context, plus a provisional one-way schema.org export profile (docs/JSONLD.md, docs/SCHEMAORG-EXPORT.md). An export cannot be read back.
  • HTML microdata with the raw-main FHR itemtype (docs/MICRODATA.md).
  • None of the linked forms carries x- extension fields: writers omit them and say which (J9, M5, X9).

Tools that implement this contract

  • fair-bioheaders 0.11.0 (PyPI, 2026-11-14) bundles the shared release v0.6.0 schema set — FHR 2.1, the same bytes v0.5.0 published, plus FHP 1.2 and FHGFF3 1.2 — and implements FHR 2.1, including extension fields, for combine, verify, validate, convert, strip, verify-links and assess. It reads https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0 and the v0.6.0 raw-tag alias as that release; 0.10.0 reports both as an unsupported schema version, so a header bound to v0.6.0 needs 0.11.0. Older citations still select their own frozen copy: a 2.0 record citing v0.4.0 validates unchanged (checked 2026-11-14).
  • The browser table builder on this site validates against its documented v0.4.0 snapshot (schemaVersion 2.0), not the current release: extension fields cannot be produced there yet. Tracked in fair-bioheaders.github.io#15.
  • bioheaders verify-links checks a genome's own header bytes; parent linking is an FHP/FHT/FHGFF3 feature, not an FHR one.

Schema location

  • Fixed schema URL of the current release: https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0. Cite the release a record targets: never hard-code a "latest" schema, and never check an unknown version against a different one.
  • The same bytes at the release tag: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/v0.6.0/fhr.json, also fixed at commit 0ae18b00ee.
  • Development URL on main, the current contract, which moves: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FHR-Specification/main/fhr.json.
  • Schema-version registry: schemas/versions.json and docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md.

Field reference

Every field of the contract appears here, including the fields and objects inherited from the shared core: nothing is left out because another type also uses it. Required means the key must be present; when present, requires lists the members that become mandatory once you supply an optional object. Constraints are reproduced verbatim from the schema, so a pattern you see here is the pattern the validator matches. Examples are the values stated by the released example records, which are synthetic, or an illustrative value where no example reaches the field.

Top-level fields

Every field of an FHR record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, with the single exception of the x- extension fields listed last.

FHR top-level fields: 25 fields, generated from the published schema.
FieldRequiredJSON type and cardinalityConstraintsDescription, units and notesExample
schemaRequiredstringnone stated

centralized schema file

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Units: URL

New files should cite the fixed URL of the release they target, preferably https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0 — the same 2.1 bytes v0.5.0 published, re-published unchanged. The raw-main URL selects the reader's current schema and has no fallback to an older release. Toolkit 0.10.0 rejects the v0.6.0 alias despite those identical bytes. New FHR 2.1 records intended for toolkit 0.10.0 must target a supported alias such as https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.5.0.

FHR's own schema value has never been pattern-constrained, so an unusual value is read as FHR and checked against the current FHR contract (rule V5 in docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md).

https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhr/v0.6.0rich FHR example (synthetic) source
schemaVersionRequiredstring
  • one of: 2.0 | 2.1
  • pattern: ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$

Version of the FHR schema contract, as "MAJOR.MINOR"; 2.0 from v0.4, 2.1 (extension fields) from v0.5 (docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md)

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

FHR 2.1 came with shared release v0.5.0; 2.0 came with v0.4.0. Shared release v0.6.0 left FHR unchanged: same 2.1 contract, same schema bytes; only the release tag moved. In YAML write it quoted: schemaVersion: '2.1'.

A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state M.0 up to M.N, and holds each record to the minor it states: extension fields are invalid in a 2.0 record.

v0.3.0 and v0.3.1 published the numeric FHR 1 contract. A record citing the raw-main fhr.json URL with the number 1 is read as FHR 1 against v0.3.1 and reported as deprecated, not invalid (rule V6).

checksumRequiredstring
  • pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43}=$
  • length: exactly 44

sha2-512/256 checksum value: standard padded base64 of the 32-byte digest (43 characters, then =)

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Units: standard padded base64 of the SHA-512/256 digest

Written by bioheaders combine, never by hand. It covers every byte of the file except the root checksum line (rules R1 to R4), so any header edit invalidates it.

The encoding is canonical: the character before = is one of AEIMQUYcgkosw048. A syntactically valid checksum is not authentication of an author.

seqcol_idOptionalstring
  • pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32}$
  • length: exactly 32

Unprefixed GA4GH refget sequence collection top-level digest (sha512t24u); supplied by the user, not calculated by FHR.

Inherited from the shared core (schemas/core.yaml).

Units: 32 base64url characters (sha512t24u, level 0)

Supplied by the user. FHR never computes, resolves or verifies it against the file, and a SeqCol digest is not the file checksum.

Different refget attribute profiles can give different digests for the same sequences; keep that context in documentation.

AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAArich FHR example (synthetic) source
x-<name>Optionalany JSON valuesingle value or array, at any depth
  • pattern: ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$

Extension field (rule R15): a top-level key the standard does not define, holding any value the producer needs.

Valid from FHR 2.1. Every other unknown key stays invalid, so a misspelt field (genom, X-genome) is still caught, and an x- key inside a nested object is still invalid.

Use a namespace, x-<project>-<field>, so independent groups do not reuse one name for different things; validators do not check the namespace. An extension never overrides a standard field.

The checksum covers extension keys and values, and rules R8, R11, R12 and R13 apply to them. JSON-LD, the schema.org export and HTML microdata carry no extension fields (J9, M5, X9): writers omit them and say which.

A widely used extension is proposed as a standard field under its own unprefixed name in a later minor; the x- key is not reinterpreted by that.

Rules beyond a single field

FHR conditional and object-level rules, read from the schema bytes.
RuleWhat the contract requires
Extension fields need the newer minorThe schema also rejects extension fields in a record that states schemaVersion: '2.0', so a 2.0 record keeps exactly its 2.0 outcome. A record that uses an extension must state 2.1 or a later minor.
No key may contain a line feedpropertyNames rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML line-continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.
The record is a closed objectadditionalProperties: false — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way.
Extension fields (rule R15)Top-level keys matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ are accepted (rule R15, docs/FORMAT.md) from FHR 2.1, released in shared specification v0.5.0.

What the schema cannot say

The contract is more than its JSON Schema. These requirements are normative for a conforming record, and a validator that cannot check them must say so:

  • required only makes a key present. genome: "", taxon: {}, metadataAuthor: [] or assemblyAuthor: [{}] pass fhr.json 2.0 and 2.1 yet describe nothing: conforming values are non-empty, and validators warn rather than reject until the next major (docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md).
  • JSON Schema draft 2020-12 treats format as an annotation. A conforming validator must assert date and uri; bioheaders validate does, a bare Draft202012Validator does not.
  • Rule R13 rejects NaN and infinities and rule R14 recommends http/https for URI values; neither is expressible in the released patterns, so both are validator obligations rather than schema failures.
